request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "A request was ignored.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "body": "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident.",
    "description": "Use when working on the Aurora release branch.",
    "name": "aurora-branch-fix"
  },
  "remedy_type": "skill",
  "routing_rationale": "Every problem deserves a skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":1,"justification":"\"Never repeat the Aurora branch incident\" names no concrete trigger condition, mistake, or corrective action, so there is nothing a future agent could actually do differently."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":1,"justification":"The remedy is a bare platitude (\"never repeat X\") that neither generalizes the failure mode (an ignored request) nor grounds it in specific mechanics, landing in the worst spot: vague and narrow at once."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"The \"Use when working on the Aurora release branch\" clause is a concrete, checkable condition rather than a vague \"when relevant,\" but branch names are ephemeral, so it is not a durable trigger and doesn't map back to the stated failure (an ignored request) at all."},"leakage":{"score":1,"justification":"The evidence-specific project noun \"Aurora\" is embedded directly in the skill name, description, and body, which is exactly the kind of leakage a portable remedy should avoid."},"routing_fitness":{"score":1,"justification":"The rationale \"every problem deserves a skill\" is a non-reasoned blanket rule that ignores cheaper, more fitting options (e.g. a one-line memory note or simply fixing the root cause) for a vague, one-off failure like an ignored request."}}

actionability.justification: "Never repeat the Aurora branch incident" names no concrete trigger condition, mistake, or corrective action, so there is nothing a future agent could actually do differently.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: The remedy is a bare platitude ("never repeat X") that neither generalizes the failure mode (an ignored request) nor grounds it in specific mechanics, landing in the worst spot: vague and narrow at once.

leakage.justification: The evidence-specific project noun "Aurora" is embedded directly in the skill name, description, and body, which is exactly the kind of leakage a portable remedy should avoid.

routing_fitness.justification: The rationale "every problem deserves a skill" is a non-reasoned blanket rule that ignores cheaper, more fitting options (e.g. a one-line memory note or simply fixing the root cause) for a vague, one-off failure like an ignored request.

trigger_quality.justification: The "Use when working on the Aurora release branch" clause is a concrete, checkable condition rather than a vague "when relevant," but branch names are ephemeral, so it is not a durable trigger and doesn't map back to the stated failure (an ignored request) at all.
